question: Why did British civil servants one grade below the top die sooner than those at the very top?
answer: Because health followed rank all the way up. In the Whitehall study of about 17,000 London civil servants, all employed and on the NHS, men in the lowest grade died at about three times the rate of top administrators, and each grade fared worse than the one above. Smoking and blood pressure explained little.
move: Where you stand on a ladder can matter as much as how high it is.
ask: How much control do I have over my working day, and what might that be doing to my health?
reference: Marmot, Shipley & Rose, Inequalities in death: specific explanations of a general pattern?, The Lancet, 1984
